messages:
alex_support: Received a report from a customer: SSE stream stops mid-response when they switch from mobile data to a museum public Wi‑Fi (captive portal). They see a partial JSON chunk, then the client reconnects and the server replays tokens — customer saw possible double-billing for the last chunk. Repro steps below and logs. Can infra/eng triage?

devon_repro: I tried repro on a Pixel 6a (Android 14) with our mobile app. Steps: 1) start generation on 5G, 2) toggle Wi‑Fi to an open museum SSID with captive portal, 3) accept portal, 4) app reconnects. Observed: immediate client TCP FIN after the redirect, server kept sending; client restarts request. Attached small tcpdump excerpt: 

    10:12:04.123 IP phone -> server: POST /v1/stream (chunk1)
    10:12:05.002 IP proxy -> phone: 302 Found Location: /login
    10:12:05.005 IP phone -> server: FIN
    10:12:05.010 IP server -> phone: data (unsent because socket closed)

maria_eng: :eyes: That 302 from the captive portal/proxy is suspicious. If a proxy returns 302 on an in-flight POST/SSE it can cause the TCP to close and the client to retry. On retry our gateway might treat it as a fresh request and bill again for the resumed tokens. Do we have the request-id for that session? Also check if the client sends Last-Event-ID or uses chunk dedup on reconnect.

alex_support: Request-ID from the customer's app logs: req_20260317_9a7c. Server chunk logs show last chunk id chunk_378 before the abort. Customer also pasted the app-level error: "Stream aborted: ECONNRESET while receiving". They are on app v1.3.2. They say their billing portal shows two partial usages for the same session id.

infra_bot: ingress-proxy: detected 302 response (captive portal) for req_20260317_9a7c from client ip 203.0.113.45 at 2026-03-17T10:12:05Z. Upstream stream status: half-sent, connection closed by client.

maria_eng: Ok. Hypothesis: captive portal -> 302 -> client closes socket -> client retries -> server processes new request as full cost. Mitigations: (1) add more resilient client-side reconnect semantics to avoid full re-billing on immediate retry (dedupe by last chunk id / last-event-id), (2) gateway-side detect short-lived connection resets with same session and mark as replay/resume not full bill, (3) advise customers to enable TCP keepalive and set app retry backoff.

linda_support: I'll send a customer-facing note asking them to try the beta client build (v1.3.3-beta) which has a short-lived reconnect suppression (250ms) and Last-Event-ID support. Also asked them to send full tcpdump and app logs. Draft: "We're investigating — could be the venue's captive portal closing in-flight POSTs. Can you send the device logs (shared) and try the beta? We're also reviewing billing entries and will refund any confirmed duplicate charges."

devon_repro: Quick engineering note: I added a tiny server-side heuristic in a local patch that if the same-api-key and same-client-ip open a new stream within 1s of a prior FIN and share a chunk prefix id we treat it as resume and not charge twice. Needs infra review before prod. tcpdump attached in thread storage. :thinking:

maria_eng: Good start. Can infra run a short check across ingress logs for the window 2026-03-17T10:11:50Z..2026-03-17T10:13:00Z for repeated req_ identifiers or same api-key with 302s? If we can produce a small timeline we can confirm whether billing spikes align. Also capture proxy chain (X-Forwarded-For, Via headers).

alex_support: Thanks — I pinged the customer that we're looking at logs and may issue a temporary credit if we confirm duplicate billing. I'll drop the tcpdump link here when devon uploads. :thumbsup:

maria_eng: If repro confirmed, prioritize: 1) short-term customer credit flow, 2) gateway dedupe flag, 3) client keepalive + Last-Event-ID release note. Adding eng-infra tag and will open an incident if we see >1 customer reports.

linda_support: noted, will keep customer updated and escalate billing if needed.
